questions.q: What does the Show Me panel actually do?
options: It highlights chart types possible with your currently selected fields and arranges them onto the same shelves you'd use manually
It writes SQL queries behind the scenes that only advanced users can see
It automatically cleans and reshapes your underlying data source
It permanently locks the chart type so it can never be changed again
questions.explain: Show Me is a recommendation panel — it looks at your selected fields, grays out impossible chart types, and rearranges the same Columns/Rows/Marks mechanics for you.

questions.q: In the exercise's finished view, what does placing Region on Color in the Marks card create?
options: A color legend, splitting each bar into segments by Region
A new numeric axis for Region
A second worksheet tab automatically
A live database connection to Region data
questions.explain: Color on the Marks card, given a discrete field like Region, produces a legend and splits marks into colored segments.

questions.q: Why does the guide suggest also building the same view manually without Show Me?
options: To prove the Columns/Rows/Marks mechanics from earlier lessons are what's really driving the chart, not something magical Show Me does
Because Show Me only works with Sample Superstore and no other dataset
Because Show Me is being deprecated in future Tableau versions
Because manual building always produces a different, more accurate chart
questions.explain: The point of rebuilding manually is to confirm that Show Me is just automating the same shelf-based mechanics covered in Lessons 1-5, not a separate system.

questions.q: What kind of field is YEAR(Order Date) in this exercise's Columns shelf, if left continuous?
options: A continuous field, creating a numeric-style axis running across years
A discrete field, creating one header per year with no axis
Neither a Dimension nor a Measure
A calculated field that must be written manually
questions.explain: As set up in this exercise, YEAR(Order Date) is used continuous, producing a true axis across the year range rather than separate discrete headers.

questions.q: What should you do if your build doesn't match the screenshot on the first try?
options: Undo (Ctrl/Cmd+Z) and try again — trial and error is expected for a first hands-on exercise
Immediately reinstall Tableau Desktop
Give up on Show Me entirely for the rest of the course
Assume the dataset is corrupted and re-download it
questions.explain: This is a first hands-on exercise — undoing and retrying is the expected, normal way to work through it.
